output.summary:
Deterministic verdict (unchanged by this advice): run_validity = VALID; policy_verdict = NO_POLICY; analysis_coverage = INCOMPLETE with reasons CAPACITY_GUARD_FAILED and CAPACITY_STAGE_NOT_VERIFIED; capacity bound_type = INDETERMINATE with lower_inclusive = null, upper_exclusive = null, capacity_knee = null (KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED).

The run contains a single capacity stage on the "users" load axis: d16-cpu-limited-20users, target 20, achieved 20 (achieved_statistic p05_10s), observed_min = observed_max = 20, complete_bins 30 of 30 expected, verdict INDETERMINATE, verified_bound_load = null, reason CAPACITY_GUARD_FAILED. The reason is a generator guard: a resource rule on generator-cpu-throttle-ratio with operator gt, threshold 0.2, effect "diagnostic", status FAIL. The supporting series reports mean ≈0.861, median 1, max 1, min 0.05 over 30 of 30 cells, and one resource_threshold_violation finding covering 27 cells with observed_min ≈0.3958 and observed_max 1. By contract this guard is diagnostic: its failure makes the stage unusable for a product bound and never creates an upper bound. The remedy available to an operator is a rerun with a generator that is not saturated, not a change to the guard's effect.

The window policy summary for the same window reports business_verdict PASS, resource_verdict NO_POLICY, verdict PASS. The PASS rests on exactly one policy check in the evidence: overall-errors, error_rate_ratio lte 0.01, observed numerator 0 over denominator 38842, status PASS. No latency rule and no resource rule for frontend, checkoutservice, or paymentservice appears in the evidence, so the reported latencies (overall p50 103 ms, p95 299 ms, p99 600 ms, max 1299 ms; home p95 390 ms, p99 806 ms) and the low observed CPU/memory values are unjudged rather than acceptable — missing policy is not a pass.

resource_binding records clock_alignment = "not_verified_by_core", so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal relationship between generator throttling and request latency can be supported from this analysis; clock verification is the prerequisite for any such claim.

Highest-value next steps: (1) rerun the same scenario with an unsaturated generator and confirm generator-cpu-throttle-ratio stays at or below 0.2 across the window; (2) configure a capacity policy/required capacity on the users axis plus resource rules for the system entities, since NO_POLICY becomes PASS or FAIL only through configuration; (3) add latency policy rules; (4) verify clock alignment. Nothing in this advice alters the deterministic verdict.
